<thought>Based on the observed isotopic pattern—a dominant monoisotopic peak with an M+1 intensity of ~5.6 % and rapidly decreasing higher‑mass peaks—the pattern matches the natural abundance of 13C (≈1.1 % per carbon). The magnitude of the M+1 peak suggests roughly five carbon atoms, while there is no evidence of the characteristic 3:1 (Cl) or 1:1 (Br) patterns, nor the larger M+2 contributions expected from sulfur or chlorine. Therefore, carbon is the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
